title: Hashimoto and Togami climb after Muscat titles as Lin Shidong returns to the world top 10
seo_title: World rankings week 48: Togami 11th, Lin Shidong back in top 10
description: Shunsuke Togami rises four places to 11th and Honoka Hashimoto to 13th after WTT Star Contender Muscat, while Lin Shidong swaps places with Alexis Lebrun.
standfirst: Kaho Akae, the beaten women's finalist in Oman, jumps 10 places to 26th, and the only change in either top 10 comes without a ball being hit.

body: Shunsuke Togami and Honoka Hashimoto have climbed the world rankings after winning WTT Star Contender Muscat, and Lin Shidong is back in the men's top 10 at ninth, one place ahead of Alexis Lebrun.

The ITTF ranking for week 48, published on Monday, is the first to include the points from Oman. Togami moves up four places to 11th on 3,273 points, 425 more than a week ago, and Hashimoto rises one place to 13th on 3,374, a gain of 320.
## Lin Shidong back in without playing

The only change in either top 10 came without a match. Lin did not play in Muscat and his total stayed at 3,686 points, but Alexis Lebrun's fell by 120 to 3,630, which drops the Frenchman to 10th. Félix Lebrun stays third despite losing 300 points, still 262 clear of Wang Chuqin in fourth.

Sora Matsushima remains world No 1 on 7,598 points, his eighth week at the top, ahead of his Japan teammate Tomokazu Harimoto on 6,963. Lin's return leaves China with two men in the top 10, Wang and Lin, the same as a week ago.

Togami beat South Korea's Park Ganghyeon 6-11, 11-6, 11-7, 11-5, 16-14 in the Muscat final and dropped two games in five singles matches all week, as Eleven's [finals report](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-finals-honoka-hashimoto-shunsuke-togami-titles.html) described. It was his third WTT singles title of the year. He is now 357 points behind Alexis Lebrun and passes Patrick Franziska, who slips to 12th, with Zhou Qihao, Wen Ruibo and Darko Jorgic each dropping one place.

Park, 30, climbs six places to 38th after reaching his first WTT final above Feeder level. China's Chen Yuanyu, beaten by Togami in the semi-finals, rises five places to 24th, and South Korea's Oh Junsung, the other semi-finalist and the men's doubles champion with Lim Jonghoon, goes from 19th to 17th. Lim moves up three places to 31st.

Sun Yang, the 18-year-old qualifier who [knocked out the top seed Jorgic](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-day-four-review-results-highlights.html) on his way to the last 16, where Park beat him, climbs 94 places to 134th.

Hashimoto, the 28-year-old defender, has now won WTT Contender Istanbul and the Muscat Star Contender in consecutive weeks and gained 450 points in a fortnight, moving past South Korea's Shin Yubin into 13th. In the final she came from 2-1 down to beat her compatriot Kaho Akae 4-2, saving a game point in the sixth.

Akae, 22, is the biggest climber in the women's top 50, up 10 places from 36th to 26th on 1,390 points, 300 more than a week ago. Her run to the final included wins over Miyu Nagasaki and the top seed Satsuki Odo, and she is now Japan's ninth-highest ranked woman.

Bernadette Szőcs, the Romanian Hashimoto beat in the semi-finals, rises three places to 19th. Nagasaki moves up to 17th. Going the other way, Miyuu Kihara falls nine places to 28th after losing 595 points, and South Korea's Joo Cheonhui drops one place to 18th.

At the top, nothing moved. Wang Manyu stays No 1 on 9,265 points ahead of Sun Yingsha (8,575) and Miwa Harimoto (6,889), and the women's top 12 is unchanged, with Japan holding four of the top 10 places: Harimoto, Hina Hayata, Hitomi Sato and Odo.

The next ranking points come from the Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu, which starts on Sunday 29 November, and then the [WTT Finals Hong Kong](/events/wtt-finals-hong-kong-2026.html) from 9 to 13 December. Togami, Hashimoto, Odo and Hiroto Shinozuka are in Japan's squad for Chengdu, and every player in both top 10s is in the Hong Kong field. The full top 100 is on Eleven's [rankings page](/rankings.html).
